doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Coltrane's early bass players: Steve Davis, Reggie Workman, Art Davis
summary: He describes the revolving bass chairs, including the two-bass pairing he compared to a hornets' nest.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: So that early period with Trane, he switched bass players several times.

Well Steve Davis, I don’t know—to me it was easy. I always liked the way he played, perfect pitch all the time, he was always in tune and he always had this warm sound. He picked up Reggie Warren; he played with us and made some of the recordings I think. I can’t recall them right now, it’s a document and it’s already—I think I’ve got some of those records. Anyways, so after Reggie he had Art Davis and they used to play a two bass thing and I’d tell him, “What tune are we going to play?” and he said “(scats music)” and I’d say, “When Reggie and Art Davis play together it sounds like somebody knocked over a hornets nest!” (Laughs)
Okay (Laughs) so I presume that didn’t last too long and then you got Jimmy.
You know I said that just trying to be funny but in a lot of ways, in a club for instance, they’d both be using bows and I’d say, “There it is again!” (Laughs)
Did they say anything like that to you?
